name: anonymous-install-e2e
body: Anonymous-install e2e: the CI check that the public install channels work anonymously. `e2e/install_test.go` (`TestAnonymousPackageInstall`, with helpers such as `anonymousEnv`/`installedVersion`) runs the real package-manager install — on macOS, Homebrew tap (`brew tap really-knows-ai/kalide https://github.com/really-knows-ai/kalide`), then the tap-level trust step `brew trust really-knows-ai/kalide`, then `brew install kalide`; on Windows, Scoop bucket + `scoop install kalide` — or the anonymous release download (Linux) with the GitHub token env vars (`GITHUB_TOKEN`, `HOMEBREW_GITHUB_API_TOKEN`, `KALIDE_GITHUB_TOKEN`) cleared, and asserts the installed `kalide` reports the expected version. The macOS setup runs `brew trust really-knows-ai/kalide` before `brew install kalide` (Homebrew 6.0.0+ refuses to load a formula from an untrusted custom-remote tap; the trust step satisfies that). It is wired into CI by the `package-install-e2e` job in `.github/workflows/release.yml` (owned by solution.component.release-workflow), which runs `go test ./e2e -run TestAnonymousPackageInstall` after the manifest commit, while the native-binary init/start e2e (TestNativeRelease) runs in solution.component.native-e2e-ci. It covers global.constraint.anonymous-install and the homebrew-install / scoop-install / linux-install acceptance criteria.
